nodes.summary: The distribution with probability $1/3$ on each profile of Chicken except (stay, stay) is a correlated equilibrium. A player told to leave believes the other leaves or stays with equal probability, and leaving gives it $\frac12 5 + \frac12 3 = 4$ against $\frac12 6 = 3$ for staying; a player told to stay knows the other leaves, and staying gives $6 > 5$.
nodes.title: Aumann's correlated equilibrium of Chicken

nodes.summary: Aumann's correlated equilibrium of Chicken gives probability $0$ to (stay, stay), while each player stays with probability $1/3$; so it is not the product of its marginals and is not a mixed Nash equilibrium. (It is not even a mixture of Nash equilibria, Hart and Mas-Colell 2000, §2, which is not formalised here.)
nodes.title: Chicken's correlated equilibrium is not a product

nodes.summary: The distribution on profiles of Chicken that puts probability $1/3$ on (leave, leave), (leave, stay) and (stay, leave), and $0$ on (stay, stay).
nodes.title: Aumann's correlated distribution for Chicken

nodes.summary: Chicken in cost form: each of two players chooses *leave* (strategy $0$) or *stay* (strategy $1$), with payoffs $(5,5)$ for (leave, leave), $(3,6)$ for (leave, stay), $(6,3)$ for (stay, leave) and $(0,0)$ for (stay, stay); costs are their negatives.
nodes.title: The game of Chicken

nodes.summary: The average conditional regret is a linear functional of the empirical distribution $z_T$ of play: So the regrets depend on the history only through $z_T$, which is the first step of the proof of Hart and Mas-Colell's Proposition.
nodes.title: Conditional regrets are linear in the empirical distribution

nodes.summary: After rounds with realised profiles $s(1), \dots, s(T)$, the conditional regret of player $i$ for $j \to k$ is the total cost it would have saved by playing $k$ in every round in which it played $j$: Divided by $T$ this is Hart and Mas-Colell's $D_T(j, k)$ in cost form; its positive part is the regret $R_T(j, k)$ of (2.1c).
nodes.title: Conditional regret

nodes.summary: For every $\varepsilon$, the set of correlated $\varepsilon$-equilibria is convex: the conditions $\psi \ge 0$, $\sum_s \psi(s) = 1$ and the correlated equilibrium inequalities are all linear in $\psi$.
nodes.title: The set of correlated equilibria is convex

nodes.summary: For every $\varepsilon$, the set of correlated $\varepsilon$-equilibria is closed in $\mathbb R^S$, as an intersection of finitely many closed half-spaces and hyperplanes.
nodes.title: The set of correlated equilibria is closed

nodes.summary: Summing the correlated $\varepsilon$-equilibrium inequalities of player $i$ over the recommended strategy $j$ gives the coarse inequality for the fixed deviation $k$, with error $|S_i|\,\varepsilon$: In particular every correlated equilibrium is a coarse correlated equilibrium, that is, lies in the Hannan set. The two sets coincide when every player has at most two strategies (Hart 2005, §10.1; not formalised here).
nodes.title: Correlated equilibria are coarse correlated equilibria

nodes.summary: For every $\varepsilon$, the set of correlated $\varepsilon$-equilibria is compact: it is a closed subset of the simplex of probability distributions on the finite set of profiles. Together with convexity, this makes it a convex polytope, cut out of the simplex by finitely many linear inequalities. It is nonempty for $\varepsilon \ge 0$ (it contains the Nash equilibria, which exist by Nash's theorem, or directly by…
nodes.title: The set of correlated equilibria is compact

nodes.summary: If $s^\circ$ is a pure Nash equilibrium, the point mass at $s^\circ$ is a correlated equilibrium: the only nonzero term of each correlated equilibrium sum is $c_i(s^\circ) - c_i(k, s^\circ_{-i}) \le 0$.
nodes.title: A pure Nash equilibrium is a correlated equilibrium

nodes.summary: After $T \ge 1$ rounds, the empirical distribution of play is a correlated $\varepsilon$-equilibrium if and only if every conditional regret is at most $T\varepsilon$, that is, every average regret $D_T(j, k)$ is at most $\varepsilon$. This is the finite-horizon form of Hart and Mas-Colell's Proposition: $\limsup_T R_T(j, k) \le \varepsilon$ for all players and $j \ne k$ if and only if $z_T$ converges to the set of…
nodes.title: No conditional regret characterises correlated equilibria

nodes.summary: For mixed strategies $\sigma_i$, the product distribution $\prod_i \sigma_i(s_i)$ is a correlated equilibrium if and only if no player can lower its expected cost by switching to a pure strategy, that is, if and only if $\sigma$ is a mixed Nash equilibrium. Summing the correlated equilibrium sums $\sigma_i(j)(\bar c_i(j) - \bar c_i(k)) \le 0$ over $j$ gives $\mathbb E_\psi[c_i] \le \bar c_i(k)$; the other direction…
nodes.title: The product correlated equilibria are the Nash equilibria

nodes.summary: If the mixed profile $\sigma$ is a Nash equilibrium of the game with payoffs $u_i$ (no player can raise its expected payoff by changing its mixed strategy), then the product distribution $\prod_i \sigma_i(s_i)$ is a correlated equilibrium of the game with costs $-u_i$. This applies Nash equilibria are correlated equilibria to the deviations to pure strategies.
nodes.title: Mixed Nash equilibria are correlated equilibria

nodes.summary: If no player can lower its expected cost by switching from its mixed strategy $\sigma_i$ to a pure strategy, the product distribution $\prod_i \sigma_i(s_i)$ is a correlated equilibrium. Indeed every pure strategy in the support of $\sigma_i$ then has the minimal expected cost, so each correlated equilibrium sum $\sigma_i(j)(\bar c_i(j) - \bar c_i(k))$ is nonpositive.
nodes.title: Nash equilibria are correlated equilibria

nodes.summary: A probability distribution $\psi$ on the strategy profiles of a finite game with costs $c_i$ is a correlated $\varepsilon$-equilibrium if for every player $i$ and all strategies $j, k$ of $i$ and a correlated equilibrium when $\varepsilon = 0$. Think of a referee who draws $s$ from $\psi$ and tells each player only its own coordinate $s_i$: a player told to play $j$ cannot gain by playing $k$ instead, provided the…
nodes.title: Correlated equilibrium

nodes.summary: If every $\sigma_i$ is a probability vector, so is $\prod_i \sigma_i(s_i)$: $\sum_s \prod_i \sigma_i(s_i) = \prod_i \sum_{a} \sigma_i(a) = 1$.
nodes.title: The product distribution is a distribution

nodes.summary: Given nonnegative regrets $\lambda(j, k)$ of a player for switching from $j$ to $k$, a mixed action $q$ is regret-invariant if the regret flowing into each strategy equals the regret flowing out of it: Equivalently, $q$ is an invariant probability vector of the stochastic matrix with off-diagonal entries $\lambda(j, k)/\mu$ for $\mu$ large. Foster and Vohra's calibrated forecasts use the same conservation…
nodes.title: Regret-invariant mixed action

nodes.summary: Changing player $i$'s coordinate of a profile does not change the weight $\prod_{l \ne i} \sigma_l(s_l)$ of the opponents' part.
nodes.title: The opponents' weight ignores the own coordinate

nodes.summary: For mixed strategies $\sigma_l$ and a player $i$, the weight of the opponents' part of a profile $s$ is $w_i(s) = \prod_{l \ne i} \sigma_l(s_l)$.
nodes.title: Weight of the opponents' profile

nodes.summary: $\prod_l \sigma_l(s_l) = \sigma_i(s_i) \prod_{l \ne i} \sigma_l(s_l)$ for every player $i$.
nodes.title: Splitting the product weight

nodes.summary: The product distribution of mixed strategies $\sigma_i$ is $\psi(s) = \prod_i \sigma_i(s_i)$: the law of the profile when the players randomise independently.
nodes.title: Product distribution of mixed strategies

nodes.summary: The expected cost of the pure strategy $a$ of player $i$ when the others play the mixed strategies $\sigma_l$ independently is
nodes.title: Expected cost of a pure strategy against mixed opponents

nodes.summary: For every function $f$ of profiles, $\sum_{s :\, s_i = j} f(k, s_{-i}) = \sum_{s :\, s_i = k} f(s)$: replacing player $i$'s coordinate by $k$ is a bijection from $\{s_i = j\}$ onto $\{s_i = k\}$.
nodes.title: Moving a recommendation event

nodes.summary: If the mixed action $q$ is regret-invariant for $\lambda$, then for every vector $g$ of payoffs Taking for $\lambda$ the current regrets and $g = u_i(\cdot, s_{-i})$ for an arbitrary opponents' profile, this is Blackwell's condition (3.3) for approaching the nonpositive orthant of regret vectors, with equality. It is the algebraic core of the proof of Theorem A of Hart and Mas-Colell: regret-invariant play drives…
nodes.title: Blackwell's condition for regret-invariant play

nodes.summary: For a distribution $\psi$ on profiles, $\sum_s \psi(s)\, g_i^{j\to k}(s) = \sum_{s :\, s_i = j} \psi(s)\,\bigl(c_i(s) - c_i(k, s_{-i})\bigr)$: the sum used in the definition of correlated equilibria is the sum over the event $\{s_i = j\}$ of Hart and Mas-Colell's Definition.
nodes.title: Correlated-equilibrium sums over a recommendation

nodes.summary: For the product distribution $\psi$ of mixed strategies $\sigma$, where $\bar c_i$ are the expected costs of pure strategies against the others' mixed strategies. So a product distribution is a correlated equilibrium exactly when every strategy that $\sigma_i$ plays with positive probability is a best response.
nodes.title: Correlated-equilibrium sums of a product distribution

nodes.summary: Under the product distribution of mixed strategies $\sigma$, player $i$'s expected cost is the $\sigma_i$-average of the expected costs of its pure strategies: $\mathbb E_\psi[c_i] = \sum_a \sigma_i(a)\, \bar c_i(a)$.
nodes.title: Expected cost under a product distribution

nodes.summary: In a finite game with costs $c_i$, the gain of player $i$ at the profile $s$ from playing $k$ whenever it is told to play $j$ is With payoffs $u_i = -c_i$ this is the bracket $u_i(k, s_{-i}) - u_i(s)$ of the correlated equilibrium inequalities, restricted to the event $\{s_i = j\}$.
nodes.title: Gain from a switched recommendation
